cultural.vision_reason: A carved wooden grease bowl in the form of a seal, with typical Northwest Coast formline-style incised and relief carving on the body — a classic Haida wood-carving tradition object (mislabeled "ceramic" but clearly wood, not clay).

physical.title: dish; bowl
physical.summary: Dish or bowl, for grease, made of alder, in the form of a seal. The body of the bowl is roughly oval, or perhaps ogee, in shape, decorated with incised and low relief designs indicating for instance the flippers, the head, tail and tail flippers are carved 3-dimensionally. Both the underside of the head and tail have been carved away to lighten the feel of the bowl, and the interior has been carefully cut away to leave an eye-form shape [no doubt of abstract or practical rather than symbolic significance] in the interior. The grease is caked so thick that the interior wood has disappeared, leaving the bowl with a matt black surface that emphasises the superb plasticity of the design.
